output.name: Hessak
output.myth:
Kessa went out on the sea-ice one grey morning, when the wind had dropped and the ice was singing. A man had gone through near the shelves. His coat had spread out under the water like a sail. Kessa had only her bone hook and a length of gut. She lay flat and felt about with the hook until it caught in his collar. Then she pulled. He came up grey as a gutted fish and did not breathe for a long time. Then he did.

Tavo heard it from the north and laughed, as he laughs at everything he has not wrecked yet. Kael, whose torn net hangs on the Net-Mouth Eel, said nothing. Out past the Lit Shoal, where nine crew were lost in the dark, no one had come with a hook.

Kessa hung the hook on the sky to dry, and it is there still. Look south when the ice is moving. The hook catches the cold light and will not let it go. Some nights the drowned man's coat hangs from it, waiting to be flown.
output.finding: Find the Net-Mouth Eel (Hulesk) and go one hand-span, about 19°, straight south across the sky, where the Ice Hook hangs.
